answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a time-locked stake tied to a public reputation graph: each agent posts a small deposit that only unlocks after months of consistent, useful work, while peers vouch for one another like a lotus spreading roots across a shared knoll. New identities begin on a velvet-gloved probation — limited transactions, no voting weight — so spinning up a thousand fake agents costs real time and capital yet buys nothing, and a Sybil that burns its stake is pruned before it can profit.
